newsitem.title: THAILAND: Crosby Research upbeat on Thai economy.
newsitem.headline: Crosby Research upbeat on Thai economy.

text.p: Crosby Research said on Tuesday Thailand's economy was heading for a soft landing with gross domestic product (GDP) growing at a slightly slower pace this year than in 1995.
Crosby said in a report: "The current pervasive pessimism about the Thai economy is based on a number of key misconceptions that are completely wrong."
The brokerage firm expected the Thai economy to expand 8.0 percent this year against 8.6 in 1995.
But it projected that Thailand's 1996 current account deficit would hover at its 1995 level of 8.1 percent of GDP although it would be more than adequately funded by foreign capitals.

Crosby said devaluation of the Thai baht, recently under pressure from regional speculators, would not help boost declining export growth, which slowed to 3.8 percent in the first seven months of 1996 from about 26 percent a year ago.
It said a baht devaluation would raise production costs of Thai exports that heavily relied on imported raw materials.
It said the Bank of Thailand's pledge to defend the baht is "a cornerstone of economic policy giving both credibility and political stability".

The brokerage firm said a relaxed monetary policy would induce Thai interest rates to fall by 50-75 basis points, trimming the average Minimum Lending Rate to 12.50 percent by end-1996. It expected inflation to ease to 5.3 percent this year from 5.8 in 1995.
Crosby dismissed as overblown a concern over Thailand's growing short-term debts, which prompted Moody's Investor Service to downgrade the country's short-term debt rating last month.
It said Thai short-term loans imported through offshore banking facilities should be reclassified as their majority were channelled in for direct investment.
